newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer eyes smaller Buba branch network.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer eyes smaller Buba branch network.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that the central bank planned to close more of its branches as Europe moves towards adopting a single currency.
"We strive to have some 128 branches," Tietmeyer told a news conference noting the Bundesbank had 167 branches at the end of last year and that several more have already been closed this year.
"Even with 128 branches were still have a lot more than other European central banks," Tietmeyer said.

But in the run-up to monetary union, scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999 with as many nations as meet the strict entry criteria, Tietmeyer envisioned more work would need to be handled at the Bundesbank.

As the EMU launch date approaches, Tietmeyer said that the "structure of the bank will likely remain unchanged in the near term, adding "rather we expect considerably more work" in preparing for monetary union.
Tietmeyer was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
